---
title: "Sugar Pines Sampled in Yosemite and Sequoia National Park"
format: html
---

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
library(dplyr)
library(leaflet)

# 1. Read the CSV file into R
my_data <- read.csv("2026data.csv")

# 2. define icons
tree_icons <- awesomeIcons(
  icon = "tree", # tree icon
  library = "fa", # Tells Leaflet to pull from Font Awesome
    # Pin background: red for "I", yellow for "R", light green for "CR"
markerColor = case_when(
    my_data$resistance == "I"  ~ "red",
    my_data$resistance == "R"  ~ "beige", # Golden-amber (closest to yellow in awesomeIcons)
    my_data$resistance == "CR" ~ "green",
    .default = "gray"                      # Fallback for any unexpected/NA values
  ),
  iconColor = case_when(
    my_data$resistance == "I"  ~ "#7a0000", # Dark red
    my_data$resistance == "R"  ~ "green", # Dark golden-brown
    my_data$resistance == "CR" ~ "#0b4f15", # Dark forest green
    .default = "#333333"
  ))

# 3. Pass the data frame to leaflet()
leaflet(data = my_data) |>
  addTiles() |>
  addAwesomeMarkers(
    lng = ~longitude,
    lat = ~latitude,
    icon = tree_icons,
    popup = ~paste0(
      "<b>Site ID:</b> ", plotID, "<br>",
      "<b>Tree ID:</b> ", treeID, "<br>",
      "<b>Resistance:</b> ", resistance, "<br>",
      "<b>Date collected:</b> ", date
    )
  )
```
  

<i class="fa fa-tree" style="color: #d63e2a;"></i> **Red Trees** indicate Sugar Pines infected with white pine blister rust (WPBR),

<i class="fa fa-tree" style="color: #f69730;"></i> **Beige Trees** represent Sugar Pines potentially resistant to WPBR,

<i class="fa fa-tree" style="color: #72b026;"></i> **Green Trees** represent Sugar Pines confirmed resistant to WPBR
